name: Scientific Revolution
title: The story of the Scientific Revolution

text: For nearly two thousand years, people in Europe learned from Greek thinkers that the Earth stood still at the centre of everything.
The astronomer Ptolemy had shown the planets moving around it in circles upon circles.
src: For nearly two thousand years learned people around the Mediterranean and in Europe understood nature through the works of Greek thinkers / Aristotle taught that the Earth stood still at the centre of a finite universe
The Almagest of Claudius Ptolemy, written in the 2nd century CE, gave astronomers a geometrical model of the planets, built of circles upon circles

text: Scholars began to look for surer knowledge, based on careful measuring, testing by experiment, and mathematics.
René Descartes, for example, explained the world as a machine of moving matter.
src: What many of them sought was a knowledge of nature more certain and more useful than the commentaries on Aristotle / one founded on observation and measurement, tested by experiment and, where possible, expressed in mathematics
Many hoped to explain nature as a machine / described the physical world as matter in motion acting only by contact

text: More than 450 years ago, Nicolaus Copernicus wrote that the Earth is a planet, circling the Sun each year.
With a telescope, Galileo saw mountains on the Moon and four moons circling Jupiter, and wrote a book about them.
src: which placed the Sun near the centre of the universe and made the Earth a planet, turning daily on its axis and circling the Sun each year / years: 1543 to 1687
Galileo’s Starry Messenger reports mountains on the Moon and four moons of Jupiter / built a telescope

text: Most of these scholars were believers, but they argued about how far the Church should guide the study of nature.
Galileo argued that the Earth moves, and the Church's court, the Inquisition, forced him to take it back.
src: For most of them religion was not an opponent / They argued, rather, about how far scripture and the authority of the Church should govern the reading of nature
after Galileo had argued for the Earth’s motion / the Roman Inquisition forced him to abjure

text: Isaac Newton showed that the same laws explain falling objects on Earth and the paths of the Moon and planets.
Scholars also gained new tools, such as the telescope and microscope, and societies like the Royal Society in London.
src: showed that the same three laws of motion and a single force of universal gravitation explained the fall of bodies on Earth, the orbits of the Moon and planets
Natural philosophers had gained new instruments, among them the telescope, microscope / the Royal Society was founded in London

text: Newton's work became the model of knowledge for the Age of Enlightenment that followed.
Many see it as the beginning of modern science, though it built on Greek, Islamic and medieval learning.
src: Newton’s work had become the model of knowledge for the Age of Enlightenment
The Scientific Revolution is often seen as the origin of modern science / it built on Greek, Islamic and medieval learning
